name: QuIP#: Even Better LLM Quantization with Hadamard Incoherence and Lattice Codebooks
authors: Tseng, Chee, Sun, Kuleshov, De Sa
problem: Weight-only PTQ at <=4 bits was not yet Pareto-optimal, and generic random orthogonal incoherence transforms are slow and lack tight guarantees.
mechanism: Three changes to QuIP: (1) the randomized Hadamard transform replaces the generic random orthogonal matrix - faster (O(n log n), and hardware-friendly butterfly structure) with better theoretical incoherence bounds; (2) VECTOR quantization with hardware-efficient codebooks built on the E8 lattice, which gives the optimal packing of the unit ball in 8 dimensions and exploits the ball-shaped sub-Gaussian distribution incoherent weights have; (3) a final fine-tuning stage to recover fidelity to the original model.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): outperforms existing PTQ methods at <=4 bits per weight, 'enables new behaviors in PTQ scaling', and supports fast inference. COMPRESSION RATIO: up to 8x at the 2-bit extreme. QUALITY COST: no numeric perplexity or accuracy delta appears in the abstract, so speedup_reported stays qualitative here rather than inventing a number. OpenReview search independently confirms the ICML 2024 venue.
